Child Health Nursing Internship

Child health internship — 4 weeks of supervised practice in paediatric wards: feeding, play, growth and IMNCI care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the objectives of a child health internship
  • Care for sick children and their families
  • Practise nutrition and growth monitoring
  • Use play therapy and child-friendly communication

In simple words

The child health internship trains the student to care for infants and children in the ward, keep their families at the centre, and use growth, feeding and play as tools.

Objectives

  • Apply the nursing process to sick children and their families
  • Practise feeding, nutrition and growth assessment
  • Give medicines and intravenous therapy for weight-based doses
  • Practise IMNCI assessment and care
  • Communicate with child and parent; use play therapy
  • Practise infection control and isolation for children
  • Support parents and prepare the family for discharge

Skills practised

  • Age-based communication and assessment
  • Vital signs, weight, height, MUAC, growth chart
  • Comfort and positioning
  • Paediatric medication by weight; nebulisation; oxygen; IV fluids
  • Feeding: breastfeeding support, nasogastric tube, paediatric feeds
  • IMNCI classification and danger signs
  • Isolation and infection control for children
  • Play and activity therapy; preparation for procedures
  • Discharge planning and parent counselling

🔴 Care for the child with the family

The parent is the child’s constant caregiver. Keep the parent informed, allow feeding and comfort, and use play and simple words to reduce fear.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Child health internship applies the nursing process to sick children and families.
  2. Doses and fluids are calculated by weight.
  3. IMNCI assessment uses ask, look, feel, classify and treat.
  4. Growth monitoring detects malnutrition early.
  5. Play and parent participation are part of care.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Hand hygiene and contact precautions prevent spread.
  2. Weight-based fluid therapy: hourly maintenance and deficit correction.
  3. Document growth, feeding and danger-sign education.
  4. Discharge teaching covers feeding, danger signs and follow-up.
  5. Comfort care: pain assessment and anxiety relief.

📌 Memory trick

Child-friendly care: W-P-G — Weight-based doses, Play and family, Growth monitoring.

60-second revision

  • Apply nursing process to the child and family.
  • Practise weight-based medication and fluid therapy.
  • IMNCI and danger signs.
  • Feeding support and growth monitoring.
  • Play, communication, infection control and family teaching.

Test yourself

Child doses and fluids are calculated by:

Answer: B. Paediatric medicines and fluids are calculated by body weight and confirmed by reference charts.

IMNCI assessment begins with:

Answer: A. IMNCI uses ask, look and feel to classify the child’s illness and decide the plan.

Growth monitoring detects:

Answer: B. Regular weight and height plotting detects malnutrition and growth failure early.

Which reduces fear in a sick child?

Answer: B. Play, simple words, parent presence and preparation reduce fear and cooperation.

Before discharge, parents must be taught:

Answer: A. Discharge teaching includes feeding, danger signs and the review date.
